Description: Type of model system, reflecting the terminal/end-state system for the experiment being described (or for an animal model, the overall model).
Valid Values: animal, assembloid, immortalized cell line, iPSC, microphysiological system, organoid, primary cell culture, tissue slice

Description: An animal that is amenable to experimentation and whose physiological or pathologic mechanisms are sufficiently similar to those of a human for the animal to serve as a model.
The combination of two or more distinctly patterned organoids or an organoid plus additional cell or tissue type(s).
A cell that is expected to be capable of an unlimited number of divisions, and is thus able to support indefinite propagation in vitro as part of an immortal cell line.
Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPS cells or iPSCs) are a type of pluripotent stem cell artificially derived from a non-pluripotent cell.
Devices designed to recapitulate tissue or organ-level physiology and architect by combining microfluidics; microfabrication; and 3D cell culture.

A three dimensional mass comprised of a cultured cell or tissue sample that resembles an in vivo tissue or organ. Organoids are grown in vitro from a combination of cells or tissue fragments cultured in medium containing a variety of biochemical factors.
The cells taken from a tissue source, and their progeny, grown in culture before subdivision and transfer to a sub culture.

A technology used for preclinical research as an alternative to some animal testing. Micrometer-thin slices of various organs are incubated with various experimental compounds for assays involving toxicology, absorption, distribution, and metabolism.
